> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Documentation-only change; the security content is generally accurate and matches the implementation (Temporal server next to the region controller, rackd without direct database access, snap-based installation). The dependency is valid: sphinxcontrib-mermaid 2.0.2 exists and requires Python >=3.10, while RTD uses 3.12. Two substantive gaps remain.

1. Mermaid is enabled with the default `raw` output, so the diagram is rendered client-side from cdn.jsdelivr.net (Mermaid plus D3). The `offline-docs` part of snap/snapcraft.yaml builds docs with `MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true` and ships them inside the snap, where the diagram will be blank. RTD also builds `formats: pdf`; the LaTeX visitor invokes `mmdc` (mermaid-cli), which is not installed by docs/requirements.txt, so the PDF drops the diagram. Vendor the JavaScript (`mermaid_use_local`/`d3_use_local`) or use a pre-rendered image, and add mermaid-cli if the PDF should contain the diagram.

2. The decommission guide does not cover the `maas-test-db` snap (still documented for non-production installs) or existing snapd snapshots, and its PostgreSQL/Vault cleanup bullets contain no commands, so it cannot deliver its promise of leaving no data or credentials behind. Consider also listing the OpenFGA authorization service in the architecture, since the page's entitlements section depends on it.

No runtime code changed; no tests are applicable.

docs/explanation/security.md.15: Default `mermaid_output_format` is `raw`, so this page loads Mermaid and D3 from cdn.jsdelivr.net at view time. The snap's `offline-docs` part builds docs with `MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true make html` and ships them offline, where this diagram will be blank. Vendor the scripts (`mermaid_use_local`, `d3_use_local`) or use a pre-rendered static image.
docs/explanation/security.md.51: The security architecture omits the `maas-openfga` service (`src/maasopenfga`, shipped in the snap) even though the Fine-grained authorization section below depends on it. It is a distinct process with its own PostgreSQL schema and a security-relevant trust boundary; add it to the diagram and component list, or state explicitly that it is internal to the region controller.

docs/requirements.txt.23: This only enables the HTML path. `.readthedocs.yaml` builds `formats: pdf`; for non-HTML builders sphinxcontrib-mermaid shells out to `mmdc` (mermaid-cli), which is not installed here or in the RTD image, so the PDF build emits `command 'mmdc' cannot be run` and drops the diagram. Install Node plus mermaid-cli (for example via `build.tools.nodejs` and npm) or pre-render the diagram as an image.

docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.41: Only the `maas` snap is removed. Non-production deployments use the `maas-test-db` snap (see docs/how-to-guides/back-up-maas.md), whose snap data directory holds the MAAS database; it is never removed here, so MAAS data survives. Also, `--purge` only suppresses creation of a new snapd snapshot; snapshots already in `/var/lib/snapd/snaps` are not covered by the `ls /var/snap/maas/` check. Add `snap remove maas-test-db --purge` when used, and an explicit snapshot cleanup/verification step.
docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.58: These bullets are not actionable. There are no commands for dropping the database/user, for example `sudo -u postgres dropdb maas` and `sudo -u postgres dropuser maas`, and no note that the PostgreSQL server may itself be the `postgresql` snap installed by the install guide, which must also be removed or sanitized if dedicated to MAAS. Likewise, the linked `config-vault` CLI reference only documents `configure` and `migrate`; point readers to Vault's own CLI/API commands for deleting the secrets and AppRole, otherwise the stated goal of leaving no data behind cannot be met.
